subject: Post-demo recap: first-packet latency & streaming cadence — next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@alphaedge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap: first-packet latency & streaming cadence — next steps

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed set of next steps so we can size a short pilot:

Key performance targets you confirmed on the call:
- First-packet (time-to-first-token) target: <= 120ms p50 for prompts up to ~64 tokens; p95 goal under 250ms for warm cache traffic.
- Streaming behavior: prefer a persistent WebSocket for longer sessions, but SSE is acceptable for server-driven flows.
- Chunk cadence: first chunk should arrive within target TTFT window (<=120ms), subsequent chunks ideally every 200–350ms for mid-length outputs (100–400 tokens).
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline expected concurrency ~250 active user streams, design for sustained 300 with bursts to 800 for peak shopping events.
- Average output size: ~180 tokens; token distribution attached in the spreadsheet.

Constraints we discussed worth calling out:
- You want predictable p50/p95 for short prompts (search/autocomplete) and graceful degradation for long-form generation.
- You mentioned connection reuse across requests matters for your mobile clients.

Requested materials / next steps from AlphaEdge:
1) Share a realistic sample of prompt shapes and token length distribution (you mentioned you could export a one-day sample).
2) A small network trace showing RTTs from representative client regions (attach pcap if possible) — we can use that to model cold-start vs warm-cache TTFT.
3) Confirm whether you will prioritize WebSocket for the pilot or want us to validate both SSE and WebSocket flows.

Redwood's pilot proposal (high level):
- 1-week pilot: run a dedicated pool with model variant suggestions and instrumentation to measure p50/p95 TTFT and chunk cadence.
- Engineering POC: Marissa will run the pilot engineering side; Ben will coordinate capacity estimates and pricing.
- Attachments: alphaedge_slo_matrix.xlsx (SLO hypotheses + measurement plan), sample_network_trace.pcap (placeholder).

Can you confirm the sample export and which streaming transport you want us to validate? If you prefer, I can schedule a 30-minute follow-up with Marissa and your DevOps lead to nail the pilot config.

Thanks,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Shah <priya@alphaedge.io>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Ops Team <devops@alphaedge.io>
Date: 2027-03-29T12:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: first-packet latency & streaming cadence — next steps

Dylan —

Appreciate the concise recap. Confirming the items from our side:
- The TTFT targets you listed match what we want to validate: p50 <= 120ms, p95 < 250ms for short interactions.
- For the pilot we'll prefer WebSocket (our SDK has better session management there) but we also want Redwood to demonstrate SSE performance for a comparative readout.
- Concurrency: baseline 250, planning for 4x during high-load jobs (so your burst-to-800 number is sensible).
- Typical payloads: end-user prompts average 40 tokens, model responses average ~180 tokens; occasional long-form up to 900 tokens.<

Action items from AlphaEdge: we'll provide
1) a 24-hour sample of anonymized prompts + response lengths (export attached in the secure Drive link)
2) a small tcpdump from our East US mobile edge showing median RTT ~30ms and 95th ~120ms. We'll upload an obfuscated pcap to the Drive by EOD.

Questions for Redwood before pilot kickoff:
- How does continuous batching affect TTFT for small prompts? We need to understand whether batching introduces extra latency at low qps vs single-request execution.
- If we run WebSocket, what connection lifecycle do you recommend (keep-alive interval, max idle before tear-down) to balance resource usage?

We can do a 30-minute alignment with Marissa and your infra engineer tomorrow at 10:00am PT. Does that work?

Thanks,
Priya

--
Priya Shah
Head of Product, AlphaEdge
priya@alphaedge.io
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap: first-packet latency & streaming cadence — next steps

Marissa / Ben —

Forwarding Priya's confirmation and the questions they raised. Quick internal notes and asks before our alignment call:

1) Batching behavior: we should prepare a short write-up that explains continuous batching thresholds and expected TTFT impact at low qps. Include concrete numbers for our runtime (e.g., no batching penalty for single-request exec path; batching window 1–10ms under load; but we should verify with current kernel selection).

2) WebSocket recommendations: propose keep-alive 30s, max idle 5 minutes before tear-down, and a connection pool strategy for mobile SDKs. Also mention fallback to SSE for browser-oriented flows.

3) Capacity ask: build a quick capacity sketch that maps 300 sustained / 800 burst -> GPU pool size and expected per-token cost +/- 20%. Ben, can you pull a rough estimate for a mixed 13B quantized variant and a float16 70B option?

4) Pilot instrumentation: we need to turn on prefix/KV cache hit metrics, per-token latency histograms, and chunk-gap histograms (time between chunk events) in the pilot telemetry. Add these to the SLO spreadsheet.

Priya also plans to upload a 24-hour prompt sample and a pcap. I'll have the calendar invite for the 10:00am PT slot if that works.

Thanks —
Dylan

Team —

I'll own the pilot engineering run. Proposed immediate deliverables before the kickoff call tomorrow:

- Short doc: "Batching & TTFT tradeoffs" (1 page) that explains our low-qps single-request path, batching window behavior under load, and a table with expected p50/p95 delta for a few representative prompt lengths. I'll attach it to the Drive link and email it to Priya.
- WebSocket ops guidance: recommended keep-alive 30s, idle tear-down 5m, and a client-side reconnect strategy (exp backoff with jitter).
- Capacity sketch: Ben, please add cost rows for (a) quantized 13B dedicated pool, (b) float16 70B dedicated pool, and (c) mixed fallback plan. Show expected throughput and latency SLOs mapped to #GPUs.
- Pilot telemetry template: I'll add fields for first-token p50/p95, chunk-gap median/p95, cache-hit rate, and per-request token counts.

I'll attach the one-pager and telemetry template to the HubSpot deal and the shared Drive before the call. I'll also include a short checklist for the DevOps trace we need to correlate client RTTs to observed TTFT.

If all looks good we can proceed with the 1-week pilot starting Mon 2027-04-05.

Marissa
